problem: Large Language Models (LLMs) struggle to adapt to domains where they have insufficient knowledge, such as frequently updated libraries and long-tail programming languages, because existing retrieval-augmented code generation (RACG) pipelines use static knowledge bases with a single source (p.1).
methodology: The authors developed EVOR, a pipeline that employs the synchronous evolution of both queries and diverse knowledge bases through multi-round interactions among retrievers, LLMs, and executors (p.1). EVOR constructs a knowledge soup containing web search, documentation, execution feedback, and code snippets, iteratively updating the queries and knowledge base based on execution feedback (p.1, p.3).
dataset: EVOR-BENCH, a new benchmark comprising four datasets simulating realistic RACG scenarios: Scipy-M and Tensorflow-M (modified versions of Scipy and Tensorflow libraries), and Ring and Pony (long-tail programming languages) (p.1, p.4).
results: EVOR achieves two to four times the execution accuracy compared to other methods like Reflexion and DocPrompting (p.1). Specifically, EVOR achieves an average execution accuracy of 35.3% with ChatGPT and 32.2% with CodeLlama across the four EVOR-BENCH datasets (p.5).
key_findings: Both synchronous evolution and diverse knowledge sources are critical to the success of EVOR, and EVOR can be flexibly combined with existing code generation approaches and agent-based methods to yield further performance improvements (p.2, p.6, p.7).
title: EVOR: Evolving Retrieval for Code Generation
